symptom: A synthetic interruption state after linkSync(temp, destination) but before unlinkSync(temp) preserves the complete published JSON yet leaves two hard links. Strict verifyJsonReadback then rejects the destination (nlink=2); a repeat append cannot replace it. This is a reproducible recovery/availability gap, not an observed real process crash or data loss.
lesson: Hard-link publication and temporary-name cleanup are separate operations. A durable-looking published JSON record can fail the single-link readback invariant after an interruption even though its bytes and append-only identity are preserved. Successful normal-path CI is not crash-recovery evidence.
guardrail: Keep strict single-link readback and no-replace append behavior. Before claiming crash-safe recovery, test the post-link/pre-unlink state with synthetic files, require inode-verified and scope-limited cleanup or a vetted no-replace publication primitive, and assess directory fsync and concurrent/symlink cases. Never auto-delete unverified files or relax readback globally; no production authority.
